subject: English Language Arts
standard: Cite the textual evidence that most strongly supports an analysis of what the text says explicitly as well as inferences drawn from the text.
description: Students analyze text and cite specific evidence to support their analysis and inferences.

subject: English Language Arts
standard: Write arguments to support claims with clear reasons and relevant evidence.
description: Students write persuasive texts using logical reasoning, credible evidence, and appropriate organization.

subject: Mathematics
standard: Recognize and represent proportional relationships between quantities.
description: Students identify, graph, and solve problems involving proportional relationships.

subject: Science
standard: Construct a scientific explanation based on evidence for the role of photosynthesis in the cycling of matter and flow of energy into and out of organisms.
description: Students explain how photosynthesis converts light energy to chemical energy and cycles matter through ecosystems.

subject: Science
standard: Construct, use, and present arguments to support the claim that when the kinetic energy of an object changes, energy is transferred to or from the object.
description: Students explain energy transfer and transformation using evidence and reasoning.

subject: English Language Arts
standard: Cite several pieces of textual evidence to support analysis of what the text says explicitly as well as inferences drawn from the text.
description: Students use multiple pieces of evidence from informational texts to support their understanding and analysis.

subject: Mathematics
standard: Analyze and solve pairs of simultaneous linear equations.
description: Students solve systems of linear equations using graphing, substitution, and elimination methods.

subject: Social Studies
standard: Use questions generated about individuals and groups to analyze why they, and the developments they shaped, are seen as historically significant.
description: Students analyze historical significance by asking questions about individuals, groups, and events.
